description: Composite group of two images reporting the same tensile dataset: a stress-strain plot and Table 2. The plot, labelled (b), has "Engineering strain (%)" from 0 to 50 on the abscissa (10% ticks) and "Engineering stress (MPa)" from 0 to 1400 on the ordinate (200 MPa ticks), with a legend listing as-cast (black), 723 K/3 h (red), 773 K/3 h (blue) and 823 K/3 h (green). The black as-cast curve shows the lowest plateau level but extends past the 30% gridline, approaching 40%; with increasing aging temperature the curves sit at higher stress but terminate at progressively smaller strains, the green 823 K/3 h curve failing between the 0 and 10% gridlines. Table 2 tabulates yield strength [MPa], tensile strength [MPa] and total elongation [%] as mean ± SD for 0.02Nb steels and 0.04Nb steels in the as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h states, with all stress values falling in the 880-1133 MPa band visible in (b). Together the panels make one argument: Nb addition and aging raise yield and tensile strength at the cost of ductility — 0.04Nb 823 K/3 h reaches 1056 ± 28 MPa yield strength with only 7 ± 1% elongation, versus 896 ± 23 MPa and 37 ± 2% for 0.04Nb as-cast.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves, y-axis 'Engineering stress (MPa)' 0-1400 (200 MPa ticks), x-axis 'Engineering strain (%)' 0-50 (10% ticks). Legend: as-cast (black), 723 K/3 h (red), 773 K/3 h (blue), 823 K/3 h (green). The black curve has the longest elongation (extends past the 30% gridline); the green, blue and red curves plateau at higher stress but fail at progressively shorter strains (green earliest, between the 0 and 10% gridlines).

Table titled 'Tensile mechanical properties of the Nb-containing steels' with columns Samples, Aging states, Yield strength [MPa], Tensile strength [MPa], Total elongation [%]. Eight data rows: 0.02Nb steels (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h) and 0.04Nb steels (same four aging states), each value with a ± standard deviation.

observations.observation: Panel (b) is an engineering stress-strain plot, x-axis 'Engineering strain (%)' 0-50, y-axis 'Engineering stress (MPa)' 0-1400, with legend entries as-cast (black), 723 K/3 h (red), 773 K/3 h (blue), 823 K/3 h (green).

In panel (b) the black as-cast curve reaches the lowest plateau stress but the largest strain, terminating past the 30% gridline, whereas the green 823 K/3 h curve reaches the highest stress level and fails between the 0 and 10% gridlines.

Table 2 reports columns Samples, Aging states, Yield strength [MPa], Tensile strength [MPa] and Total elongation [%] for two sample groups, 0.02Nb steels and 0.04Nb steels, each in four aging states (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h).
0.02Nb steel as-cast: yield strength 880 ± 19 MPa, tensile strength 1016 ± 12 MPa, total elongation 39 ± 2%; after 823 K/3 h: 1041 ± 15 MPa, 1125 ± 10 MPa, 8 ± 3%.
0.04Nb steel as-cast: yield strength 896 ± 23 MPa, tensile strength 1078 ± 18 MPa, total elongation 37 ± 2%; after 823 K/3 h: 1056 ± 28 MPa, 1133 ± 33 MPa, 7 ± 1%.
Within both steel groups, increasing the aging temperature from as-cast to 823 K/3 h monotonically increases yield strength and tensile strength while monotonically decreasing total elongation.
At every matching aging state the 0.04Nb steel shows a higher yield strength and higher tensile strength but a lower total elongation than the 0.02Nb steel.
The citing text states that the uniaxial tensile tests reveal that enhancing Nb content and employing aging treatment increase the yield strength, as evidenced by Figure 9 and Table 2.

The citing text states that austenite accounts for over 80 vol% volume fraction and therefore plays a dominant role in determining the mechanical properties of the low-density steels, motivating a quantitative analysis of austenite strengthening for the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.
The stress-strain panel shown here is labelled only '(b)', indicating it is one panel of a larger multi-panel figure whose companion panels are not supplied in this group.

unreadable_items: No legibility problems: all axis ticks, legend entries and table cells in the supplied images are readable.

Panel (b) carries no printed numerical data labels on the curves, so the stress-strain values can only be read qualitatively against the gridlines; the exact numbers for those curves are available only from Table 2.
